text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 12 in history.
1787 - Pennsylvania became the second state of the American Union.
1792 - Ludwig van Beethoven, aged 22 and newly arrived in Vienna, noted in his diary he had 15 ducats -- enough for his first music lesson with Franz Joseph Haydn.
1805 - U.S. transport pioneer Henry Wells born; one of the founders of the American Express Company, he teamed up with William Fargo to form the Wells Fargo Company.
1849 - French-born engineer and inventor Marc Isambard Brunel died. Father of Isambard Kingdom Brunel, his notable achievement was a breakthrough in underwater tunnelling.
1863 - Norwegian painter Edvard Munch born. His most characteristic work is the "The Scream", in which an anonymous figure on a bridge clasps his hands to his ears.
1889 - English poet Robert Browning died; husband of Elizabeth Barrett Browning, his greatest work was "The Ring and the Book".
1893 - Edward G. Robinson, U.S. film actor born in Bucharest as Emmanuel Goldenburg; he appeared in powerful gangster films such as "Little Caeser" and "Key Largo".
1896 - Guglielmo Marconi gave the first public demonstration of wireless in London. On the same day in 1901 he made the first transatlantic radio transmission from Cornwall to Newfoundland.
1911 - King George V held a coronation durbar in Delhi, where the Indian capital was to be moved from Calcutta.
1913 - The painting "Mona Lisa" was recovered in Florence after having been stolen from the Louvre two years earlier.

1915 - Singer and actor Frank Sinatra born. Known as "Ol' Blue Eyes", he won an Oscar for his role in the film "From Here To Eternity" and his best-known songs included "My Way" and "Strangers in the Night".
1915 - The first all-metal plane flew for the first time. Built by German Hugo Junkers it was known as the "Tin Donkey".
1936 - Chinese leader Chiang Kai-shek declared war on Japan.
1936 - George VI acceded to the British throne following the abdication of King Edward VIII.
1939 - Actor Douglas Fairbanks senior died. Best remembered for his swashbuckling roles in silent films, he was also a co-founder of the United Artists Corporation.
1955 - The United States closed its consulate in Hanoi following the end of the Indochina war and the partition of Vietnam.
1955 - The first prototype of the hovercraft was patented by British engineer Christoper Cockerell.
1963 - Kenya became an independent state within the Commonwealth with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister; it became a republic on the same day the following year with Kenyatta as president.
1966 - British yachtsman Francis Chichester was helped ashore in Sydney after the longest solo sea voyage in history; his ketch Gypsy Moth IV covered the 13,750 mile voyage in 107 days.
1969 - Greece withdrew from the Council of Europe -- shortly before it was to have been expelled because of its military regime.
1969 - Anarchists were blamed for bomb explosions in Milan and Rome which killed 13 people and injured more than 100.
1979 - The port of Tumaco, Colombia, was hit by an earthquake measuring 8.0 on the Richter scale; 600 died and 80,000 were made homeless.
1988 - 35 people were killed and about 150 injured when a packed commuter train piled into the back of another at Clapham Junction in south London.
1993 - Hungarian Prime Minister Jozsef Antall died in hospital after a long fight against cancer aged 61.
1993 - Eduardo Frei swept to victory in Chile's presidential elections, the first since military rule ended in 1990.
1995 - Two French airmen shot down and captured by the Bosnian Serbs in August were released.
